issues.description: revoke_error exposed on lease lookup without a documented redaction contract or capability gate
issues.detail: The PR author themselves asks whether surfacing RevokeErr is safe and ships it unresolved. Error strings from arbitrary backends routinely leak paths, endpoints, and credential fragments. Either define and enforce a redaction invariant at the point RevokeErr is written, gate exposure behind sudo/root capability, or sanitize before emit. Don't ship a public field whose contents are 'should not be sensitive'.

issues.description: Rename FetchLeaseTimes -> FetchLeaseInfo broadens the contract without restating it (and churns an exported API)
issues.detail: The new name implies general 'info' but callers still receive a partially-populated *leaseEntry with an implicit export-safe projection. The docstring does not enumerate which fields are populated vs zero. Either document the exact projection as the postcondition, return a distinct exported LeaseInfo struct, or keep FetchLeaseTimes as an alias to avoid breaking out-of-tree consumers.

issues.description: Test coverage for namespace_path and revoke_error is missing
issues.detail: TestSystemBackend_leases only asserts path. The two new fields carrying security-relevant content get zero coverage. Add a test that registers a lease in a child namespace and asserts namespace_path, and one that forces a revoke failure and asserts revoke_error shape. Otherwise the schema fields are aspirational and regressions will go unnoticed.

issues.description: OpenAPI schema marks path Required:true but the value may be empty for edge-case leases
issues.detail: leaseInfoForExport copies whatever le.Path holds, including possibly empty strings for token leases or irrevocable entries loaded from storage. If Path can legitimately be empty, Required:true is a lie and generated clients will break. Either enforce the invariant that Path is always non-empty for any lease returned here, or drop Required:true.

issues.description: Test inconsistently mixes nil context and t.Context() across touched tests
issues.detail: TestExpiration_revokeEntry_rejected_fairsharing was switched to namespace.RootContext(t.Context()) while TestExpiration_FetchLeaseTimesIrrevocable and other touched tests still pass nil. Pick one. Either the contract on ctx allows nil and should be documented, or all sites should be updated. Drive-by inconsistency confuses future maintainers.

issues.description: metrics label 'fetch-lease-times' is stale after the rename to FetchLeaseInfo
issues.detail: metrics.MeasureSince still uses the literal "fetch-lease-times" key while the function is now FetchLeaseInfo. Either keep the metric name and add a comment so the next maintainer doesn't 'fix' it, or rename it as a deliberate telemetry change. Silent mismatch between code and metric label will confuse ops.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, well-shaped contract-widening patch with two real problems. First, revoke_error is exposed on a non-privileged lookup endpoint despite the author flagging it as potentially sensitive — it needs a documented redaction invariant or capability gate before shipping. Second, the FetchLeaseTimes -> FetchLeaseInfo rename broadens the contract without restating it, churns an exported symbol, and leaves a stale metrics label. Test coverage exists only for path; namespace_path and revoke_error are untested. Ship-able after gating/sanitizing revoke_error, documenting (or reverting) the rename, fixing the metric, and adding tests for the two uncovered fields.
